themes_detail.label: Building Maintenance Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Maintenance or Facility complaints spiked to 13 THIS WEEK versus a baseline of 4.4 per week over the prior 8 weeks (197% increase, z-score 5.22), suggesting a sudden wave of deteriorating conditions across residential or commercial buildings in Tottenville/Great Kills.
evidence: 13 maintenance complaints filed THIS WEEK vs. 4.4 weekly average (197% spike)
z-score of 5.22 indicates statistically significant anomaly
Flooring/Stairs also spiked 300% last week (5 complaints vs. 1.2 avg), suggesting structural or safety issues
Elevator complaints up 1100% 3 weeks ago (3 vs. 0.2 avg), indicating cascading building infrastructure failures
reporting_angles: Interview building managers and residents: are there common issues (heating, plumbing, structural)? Is this seasonal or linked to a specific event?
Cross-reference DOB permits (737 filings in 90 days, 371 alterations): are landlords cutting corners on repairs or deferring maintenance?

themes_detail.label: Cannabis Retailer Complaints Surge
themes_detail.summary: Cannabis Retailer complaints jumped 700% LAST WEEK (3 complaints vs. 0.4 weekly average, z-score 5.42), the highest-volatility spike in the dataset, signaling either rapid retail expansion or operational violations in this district.
evidence: 3 cannabis retailer complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly baseline (700% increase, z-score 5.42)
Magnitude of spike (5.42 z-score) indicates rare event clustering
No prior pattern suggests this is newly emerging issue, not historical problem
reporting_angles: How many cannabis retailers have opened in Tottenville in the past 2 weeks? Are there zoning or licensing violations?
What specific complaints are residents filing (odor, loitering, sales to minors, parking)? Interview complainants and SLA enforcement.

themes_detail.label: Park Noise Explosion
themes_detail.summary: Noise - Park complaints exploded 3100% TWO WEEKS AGO (4 complaints vs. 0.1 weekly average, z-score 11.72), the single largest spike across all complaint categories, indicating a sudden change in park usage or events.
evidence: 4 noise complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.1 weekly average (3100% increase, z-score 11.72—highest in dataset)
Spike is isolated in time, suggesting event-driven or temporary condition change
No recent local news coverage, indicating potential coverage gap
reporting_angles: What parks saw noise complaints? Did a festival, construction project, or community event occur 2 weeks ago?
Interview Parks Dept. and nearby residents: is this a one-time event or new recurring pattern (e.g., expanded programming, illegal gatherings)?

themes_detail.label: Lot Condition Deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Lot Condition complaints surged 1500% TWO WEEKS AGO (4 complaints vs. 0.2 weekly average, z-score 5.67), suggesting vacant or underutilized parcels are becoming eyesores or public nuisances.
evidence: 4 lot condition complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.2 weekly baseline (1500% increase, z-score 5.67)
Aligns with long-standing community board budget request for 'Increase enforcement of illegal dumping laws'
South Shore Industrial Center and 4450 Arthur Kill Road development filings are in pipeline, suggesting lot vacancy awareness
reporting_angles: Identify which lots: are they vacant after demolition, contaminated brownfields, or in limbo due to development applications?
Interview Dept. of Sanitation enforcement: are these illegal dumping sites? Are they blocking residential quality of life?

themes_detail.label: Unleashed Dog Safety Incidents
themes_detail.summary: Unleashed Dog complaints jumped 500% LAST WEEK (3 complaints vs. 0.5 weekly average, z-score 3.54), indicating a sudden spike in pet safety violations that could pose risks to residents and children.
evidence: 3 unleashed dog complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.5 weekly average (500% increase, z-score 3.54)
Spike is recent and concentrated, not a long-running pattern
Corresponds with park noise spike 2 weeks ago, possibly related to increased park usage
reporting_angles: Where are incidents concentrated? Parks, streets, playgrounds? Are there problem owners or inadequate signage?
Interview residents with children: do they feel unsafe? Has NYPD enforcement been requested?
